image.why: How the Greeks pictured him: a plain boatman waiting for the dead on a funeral vase

summary.en: In Greek and Roman myth, the ferryman who carries the souls of the dead across the river into the underworld, for a coin. Virgil's Aeneid, Book VI, gave the Middle Ages its picture of him.

en: Some Greek burials included a coin, 'Charon's obol', to pay his fare
Appears in Book VI of Virgil's Aeneid
